Goals / success metrics you shared:
- p95 generation latency <= 180ms for 128 tokens (interactive assistant workload)
- Sustained throughput to support ~200 concurrent conversational sessions (target ~250 qps peak)

If I missed anything or you want to reprioritize goals, please reply and I’ll update. Otherwise Ethan will follow up with the technical deep-dive later today.

Thanks,

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@acme-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs, model reqs, and recommended topology

Hi Grace / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. I’m Ethan (SE) — below is a concise technical recap from our call plus an initial recommended deployment topology and perf estimates. I’ve attached a short PDF with the numbers and the topology diagram for your architecture review.

Summary of target SLOs (from call):
- p95 generation latency <= 180ms for 128-token outputs
- Sustained burstable throughput to serve ~250 qps peak
- Support for streaming token-by-token responses and function/tool calling in the prompt flow

Model and inference assumptions:
- Candidate model: Llama-2-Chat-70B (or comparable chat-optimized 70B family). We target a 4-bit quantized variant (gptq-style / group-wise quant) to reduce memory while retaining accuracy.
- Typical response length: 80–128 tokens (95th at 128)
- Prompt prefix size: average 400 tokens (user msg + system + context), KV cache reuse expected for short-term convo context

Performance levers we will use:
- Dedicated Redwood pool on H100/A100 (we recommend H100 where available for best latency)
- Model sharding: tensor parallelism + windowed KV cache pinned in GPU memory for hot contexts
- Continuous batching with micro-batches: target batch size 16–32 for generation to balance latency vs throughput
- Prefix / KV caching for frequently repeated system prompts to reduce end-to-end compute for typical flows
- Use of optimized kernels (flash attention / fused kernels) in our runtime; we’ll enable token-level streaming to reduce perceived latency for users

Initial quantitative estimate (conservative):
- Single H100 (1 GPU) with quantized 70B: ~60–80 tokens/sec for generation (depends on sequence lengths).
- To hit ~250 qps for 128-token requests (where each request requires ~128 tokens of generation) we need ~(250 * 128) = 32k tokens/sec capacity. At 70 tokens/sec per GPU -> ~460 GPU-equivalents naive; but with batching, caching, and quantization we reduce compute by approx 6–8x for typical conversational workloads.
- Practical recommendation: start with a small dedicated pool of 8 x H100 (or 16 x A100 if H100 unavailable) with autoscale/burst up to 32 GPUs for peak. This configuration is designed to:
  - Meet p95 latency target with micro-batching and aggressive caching for hot keys
  - Maintain headroom for spikes

Notes on topology options (attached diagram summarizes):
1) Redwood Dedicated (recommended for predictable latency + compliance):
   - Private GPU pool in a dedicated tenant. Autoscale policy for burst to shared capacity.
   - VPC peering or private link to Acme infra for low-latency ingress.
   - KMS integration for key management and audit logs enabled.
2) Hybrid (Dedicated + Private control plane):
   - Control plane in Redwood hosted; compute in customer VPC (on-prem or cloud) — good if you require strict data residency.
3) Hosted API (fastest to start):
   - Good for proof-of-concept but may require explicit SLA/contracting for PCI-sensitive workloads.

Configuration knobs we’ll tune during pilot:
- Batch size and max-concurrency per worker
- Quantization profile (4-bit group size / per-channel)
- Cache TTL and prefix caching hot-key policies
- Kernel/runtime flags tuned to H100 vs A100

Pilot proposal (2 weeks):
- Week 1: ingest sample logs, baseline measurements on representative prompts, tune batching and cache parameters
- Week 2: run a staged load test to simulate 200–300 concurrent sessions and iterate on autoscale thresholds. Produce a perf report with p50/p90/p95 latencies, token/sec, and cost per 1k requests estimate.

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Detailed perf estimate + topology diagram (attached)
- Pilot plan and timeline (attached spreadsheet)
- Estimated cost and reserved vs burst pricing scenarios

Open questions I need from your side to finalize sizing:
- Do you expect long-running conversations where context explodes beyond 2k tokens? (affects KV cache footprint)
- Are you constrained to a specific cloud region or on-prem footprint?

Next steps I propose:
- Grace: share sample anonymized logs and prompt templates (per call)
- Marissa: confirm pilot business owner and timeline
- I’ll produce a refined capacity + cost estimate by EOD tomorrow once I get the logs

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick whiteboard session if you want to walk through sharding and kernel tradeoffs.

— Ethan Park
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
